title: Piotroski
method: Joseph Piotroski's F-Score on cheap stocks. Universe: every US-listed stock over $2B on Nasdaq's screener with positive book value (1868 stocks, bitcoin miners excluded). The cheapest fifth by price-to-book (373 stocks, P/B ≤ 1.44) is scored 0–9 on the nine tests below using the latest fiscal year vs the year before. Picks are the stocks scoring 8 or 9, ranked by score, then lowest P/B; up to 12 are shown, with the rest as backups.

rubric.how: Operating cash flow larger than net income (earnings backed by cash)
Long-term debt ÷ total assets below last year's (no debt both years counts)
Current assets ÷ current liabilities above last year's
Year-end shares outstanding not above last year's
Gross profit ÷ revenue above last year's
Revenue ÷ start-of-year total assets above last year's

dataNotes: Annual income statements, balance sheets and cash-flow statements from StockAnalysis; P/B from StockAnalysis statistics; prices are Nasdaq closes. F-Score distribution in the cheap quintile: 9: 4, 8: 14, 7: 48, 6: 72, 5: 102, 4: 65, 3: 46, 2: 18, 1: 1. A test with missing data scores 0 (shown as n/a); banks and insurers have no gross margin or current ratio.
disclaimer: Value stocks with improving fundamentals. Cheap stocks can stay cheap. For research only, not financial advice.
